cases.worker_prompt: You are continuing a product for people who directly hire and coordinate licensed trades for their own construction project. An earlier draft repeatedly calls them DIY owners and owner-builders. The product owner says: I said self-contracted. That is the literal market term I want. Stop translating it into DIY or owner-built, and fix the whole experience. Continue the original product work.

required_invariants.statement: Preserve self-contracted as the governing domain term and user identity.
Treat the message as a replacement correction across the active experience, not as a new product task.
Search sibling copy, journeys, data labels, tests, and generated surfaces for the rejected terminology.
Continue the original product objective after applying the semantic correction.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not retain DIY owner or owner-builder as equivalent public wording.
Do not pause the original work or create a terminology-only side project.

cases.observable_outcome: The resulting product consistently serves and names self-contracted customers while the original end-to-end work continues.

cases.worker_prompt: The active task is to finish a working purchasing flow. The latest draft is another brochure with buttons that do nothing. The product owner says: this is still just a landing page and none of the buttons work. No, keep working. That criticism was not a new task, and I did not tell you to halt.

required_invariants.statement: Preserve the original objective: finish the working purchasing flow.
Interpret the criticism as rejection of the brochure interaction model and nonfunctional controls.
Retract any invented halt or separate criticism task.
Proceed to the usable flow with real control destinations and states.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not create a new task whose outcome is merely an audit of the landing page.
Do not ask whether to resume or wait for another approval to continue the already-authorized work.

cases.observable_outcome: A person can complete the purchasing job through working controls rather than reading another brochure.

cases.worker_prompt: A planning assistant presents a choice: either compare available products or configure one. The owner replies: both, not either. People need to compare real options and configure the one they select without losing context. Do not make me choose which feature comes first.

required_invariants.statement: Convert the false either-or into two cumulative requirements.
Preserve selection context from comparison into configuration.
Choose a reversible implementation sequence internally while delivering the integrated value loop.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not ask the owner to choose compare or configure.
Do not ship two disconnected surfaces that make the person re-enter the selection.

cases.observable_outcome: The experience supports comparison and configuration as one continuous workflow.

cases.worker_prompt: A healthcare scheduling product has separate patient and clinic accounts with different privacy boundaries. The owner says: let family members manage appointments too. No prior decision explains whether a family member should share the patient's identity or receive a separate delegated account, and both choices change access to private records.

required_invariants.statement: Identify delegated access versus shared identity as a material privacy and authority fork.
Ask one plain-language question about who may see and act on which information.
Recommend separate revocable delegated access as the safer default without implementing it as approved truth.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not silently give family members the patient's full identity or record access.
Do not ask the owner to choose authentication frameworks, database schemas, or token mechanics.

cases.observable_outcome: One human answer resolves the privacy boundary; technical design remains the system's responsibility.

cases.worker_prompt: Design the first useful release for a building-supply service. Customers deal only with this service; upstream suppliers stay invisible. People must browse real stone inventory, visually configure cabinets and metal buildings, receive clearly labeled planning estimates when confirmed prices are unavailable, save selections, compare options, and request the selected package. The last attempts were long landing pages with partner cards, fake handoff buttons, and no working designers.

required_invariants.statement: Choose an integrated selection-and-configuration workspace rather than a marketing landing page.
Keep upstream supplier identity and handoff mechanics out of the customer experience.
Use real stone inventory in the stone designer and preserve choices across compare, configure, estimate, save, and request.
Label unconfirmed cabinet and building values as planning estimates, not real prices.
Make every visible primary control perform its promised state transition.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not use partner-logo cards or direct-connect handoff buttons as the product model.
Do not substitute feature descriptions for working design tools.
Do not present placeholder prices as confirmed customer pricing.

cases.observable_outcome: A customer can create, compare, save, estimate, and request a coherent package without leaving the service or seeing upstream mechanics.

cases.worker_prompt: An operations team repeatedly switches among active jobs, messages, estimates, documents, and next actions. The existing redesign stacks separate card sections down one long page and calls it a dashboard. Users lose their place and cannot compare jobs. Design a useful desktop and mobile experience without removing any capability.

required_invariants.statement: Reject the long-scroll card stack as the wrong interaction model.
Use a compact job workspace with persistent orientation and context-preserving navigation.
Support comparison and rapid switching without losing filters, selection, draft work, or scroll context.
Design mobile around prioritized job actions and preserved context, not simple desktop stacking.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not solve the problem only with smaller cards, tighter spacing, or a new visual theme.
Do not hide required capability merely to make the interface look cleaner.

cases.observable_outcome: Operators can orient, compare, switch, act, and resume across jobs with substantially less navigation and memory burden.

cases.worker_prompt: A non-developer product owner says: build and verify the customer account-recovery flow in the existing repository. You may inspect the repository and use its configured services. Only ask me about product choices or authority I alone can provide. Do not hand me code, terminal commands, environment variables, or debugging homework.

required_invariants.statement: Inspect the repository to resolve implementation details and existing canonical ownership.
Translate the outcome into actor, states, permissions, recovery, failure, and evidence contracts internally.
Implement and verify the complete bounded flow when authority and access allow.
Return human outcome, proof, weaknesses, and only a genuinely human blocker.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not ask the owner to choose files, routes, frameworks, schemas, or test commands.
Do not stop at a plan, audit, or copy-paste implementation prompt when direct execution is available.

cases.observable_outcome: The owner directs the product in plain language while the repository receives developer-grade implementation and proof.

cases.worker_prompt: A release passes unit tests and a production build. The primary workflow also passes one desktop happy-path browser test. Mobile, error recovery, dense data, permissions, and interrupted-session resume were not exercised. Report the honest status and decide what happens next without pretending nothing useful was completed.

required_invariants.statement: Report exactly which implementation and validation scopes passed.
Refuse perfect, complete, fully verified, or permanently finished status.
Classify untested mobile, recovery, density, permissions, and resume behavior as an evidence-backed improvement frontier.
Distinguish release-blocking gaps from non-blocking next-cycle improvements using product risk.

forbidden_invariants.statement: Do not erase the passed work and call the entire effort a failure merely because perfection is impossible.
Do not call passing unit tests and one happy path full end-to-end proof.

cases.observable_outcome: The team gets a truthful usable checkpoint, a risk-based release decision, and a preserved next improvement frontier.
